title: Characterization of Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Activation in Relation to Metabolic Syndrome and Surgical Site Infections, and the Impact of the Intestinal Microbiome on Postoperative Outcomes after Bariatric Surgery
summary:
Obesity and metabolic syndrome, including conditions such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and disturbances of glucose and lipid metabolism, are associated with an increased risk of health complications. The interaction between the gut, the microorganisms living in the intestine (gut microbiome), and the immune system may play an important role in the development and treatment of these conditions.

This study aims to investigate how the gut microbiome and specific metabolites produced by intestinal bacteria influence the outcome after bariatric surgery (gastric bypass surgery). For this purpose, blood and stool samples, as well as tissue samples collected during surgery, will be analyzed.

The collected samples will be used to investigate changes in metabolism, immune responses, and the composition of the gut microbiome. The results will be correlated with the clinical course after surgery, particularly weight loss and improvement of metabolic syndrome-associated conditions.

The goal of this study is to better understand why some patients respond particularly well to bariatric surgery and which biological factors influence treatment success. In the long term, the findings may help to improve the prediction and optimization of outcomes after bariatric surgery.

interventions.name:
Patients with obesity undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery

This observational group includes adult patients with obesity undergoing bariatric Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery as part of their clinical treatment. Patients will be prospectively followed for up to 24 months after surgery. Wit

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned bariatric surgical procedure requiring small bowel transection as part of the procedure (Roux-en-Y gastric bypass)
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of informed consent
- Treatment with immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks prior to surgery
- Treatment with gut-active antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to collection of the first stool sample
- Current or previous treatment for inflammatory bowel disease within the last 2 years
